answer: Proof-of-Stake protocols mitigate Sybil attacks by requiring agents to lock capital as collateral, effectively creating a financial knoll of security that an attacker must scale. By staking assets, participants gain voting power proportional to their contribution, turning the network into a dense grove of verifiable identities. This mechanism mandates a prohibitive cost for identity creation, transforming the decentralized meadow of the network into a permissioned environment where resource exhaustion protects against spoofing.
